targets.authors: Tomz, Michael, and Robert P. van Houweling.
targets.title: The Electoral Implications of Candidate Ambiguity.
targets.evidence_quote:
This replication tests the claim from Tomz and van Houweling (2009) that risk-averse
voters will be less likely to prefer a political candidate with ambiguous policy positions.
targets.outcome_quote:
We did not find a significant probit coefficient associated with risk aversion (z
= -.274, p = .784), such that risk-averse respondents were no less likely to prefer an ambiguous candidate
to a precise candidate. Therefore, the replication of the relevant claim was unsuccessful according to the
SCORE criteria.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The report explicitly calls the replication unsuccessful under SCORE criteria; risk aversion did not predict avoidance of ambiguous candidates.
